topic: How does dynamic power allocation across beams address localized rain events while maintaining network-wide QoS requirements?
consensus_response: Dynamic power allocation across beams effectively addresses localized rain events by optimizing power distribution to maintain network-wide QoS requirements. Interbeam interference increases with power allocated, affecting system performance. Adaptive beamforming can minimize interbeam interference but requires real-time CSI and may exacerbate rain effects if not designed carefully. ML-based Power Allocation can mitigate rain effects by optimizing power distribution based on historical data and link characteristics, but requires accurate CSI. Hybrid Beamforming provides more accurate channel estimation but increases system complexity. Multi-Cell Cooperative Optimization enables coordinated power allocation across multiple cells, reducing interbeam interference and improving system capacity.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the importance of accurately determining link characteristics, such as latency and jitter, in dynamic power allocation across beams to address localized rain events while maintaining network-wide QoS requirements.
